skills.name: The eye, lenses and defects of vision

note.text:
The eye works like a camera: light enters through the cornea and pupil; the lens (a converging lens) focuses it on the retina, which sends signals to the brain through the optic nerve.
A converging (convex) lens is thicker in the middle and brings parallel rays together at the focus. A diverging (concave) lens is thinner in the middle and spreads rays out.
Defects: short sight (myopia) — a person sees near objects clearly but not far ones; the image forms in front of the retina; corrected with a diverging lens.
Long sight (hypermetropia) — far objects clear, near ones blurred; the image forms behind the retina; corrected with a converging lens.
The power of a lens in dioptres (D) = 100 ÷ focal length in cm (positive for converging, negative for diverging).

worked_example.problem: Find the power of a converging lens with a focal length of {f} cm.
